narratives.name: Orchestrating the Programme Journey from Vision to Sustained Value
narratives.description: How the programme management lifecycle coordinates four domain practices through a coherent journey from strategic vision to sustained organizational value.

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations initiating multi-project programmes face fragmented management disciplines where strategic investment, capability delivery, team coordination, and governance operate as independent concerns, creating gaps between strategic intent and operational execution that undermine programme value delivery.

The programme management lifecycle establishes a unifying orchestration framework that synchronizes all domain practices through shared phases, coordinated milestones, and cross-practice activities, ensuring that strategic investment decisions inform delivery planning, team formation supports governance needs, and benefits transition sustains realized value.

Orchestrating four domain practices through a coherent lifecycle demands continuous balancing between strategic patience and delivery urgency, between governance rigour and team autonomy, and between comprehensive coordination and proportionate overhead, with the constant risk that coordination mechanisms become bureaucratic rather than enabling.

The programme achieves its strategic objectives through a coordinated lifecycle where practices reinforce rather than impede each other, benefits are realized and sustained beyond programme closure, organizational learning from the programme experience is captured, and the orchestration model itself becomes an institutional asset for future programmes.

activities.name: Define Programme
activities.description: Establish programme governance, scope, business case, and organizational structure.

narratives.name: Translating Strategic Investment into Operational Programme Structure
narratives.description: Technique for establishing the programme through governance design, scope definition, and organizational structuring.

narrativeContexts.context: Programme definition transforms the strategic investment thesis into an actionable programme with defined governance, scope, management approach, and organisational structure, bridging the gap between portfolio-level strategy and coordinated multi-project delivery.

Begin by establishing the programme charter with formal authorisation, scope boundaries, and governance authority. Design the governance framework specifying decision-making structures, reporting requirements, and oversight mechanisms using MSP governance themes or PMI performance domains as reference. Select the management approach: fixed cadence, continuous flow, or hybrid. Design the initial team-of-teams structure selecting the organisational model based on programme context. Establish the programme's relationship to portfolio management defining how it receives strategic direction and reports progress. Determine the funding model and scope the first tranche to create a concrete starting point for coordinated delivery.

Defining the programme in isolation from portfolio strategy, leading to misalignment with organisational priorities. Over-specifying governance structures before understanding coordination needs, creating bureaucratic overhead that impedes rather than enables delivery. Selecting a scaling framework before understanding programme context, leading to framework-driven rather than context-driven coordination.

activities.name: Coordinate Cross-Practice Delivery
activities.description: Orchestrate delivery across programme practices ensuring coherent value delivery.

narratives.name: Weaving Four Domain Practices into Coherent Programme Delivery
narratives.description: Technique for integrating strategic value management, capability delivery, team operations, and governance into unified programme coordination.

narrativeContexts.context: Cross-practice coordination ensures that strategic value management, capability delivery, team operations, and programme governance function as an integrated system rather than isolated workstreams, with coordination overhead proportionate to the coordination value produced.

Establish a shared programme increment cadence ensuring all practices synchronise on the same rhythm. Implement cross-practice dependency management that identifies dependencies between practice areas beyond those within individual practices. Conduct integrated governance reviews assessing programme health across all four domains simultaneously using shared metrics providing a holistic view of programme performance. Use SAFe Solution Train mechanisms for large programmes or lighter mechanisms through shared governance forums and integrated dashboards for smaller programmes. Apply Disciplined Agile context-sensitive guidance to calibrate coordination intensity to programme coupling.

Applying heavyweight coordination mechanisms to loosely coupled practices, wasting effort without improving outcomes. Allowing coordination meetings to become status reporting sessions rather than decision-making and dependency resolution forums. Failing to adjust coordination intensity as the programme matures, maintaining early-stage overhead during steady-state delivery.

activities.name: Orchestrate Programme Benefits Transition
activities.description: Coordinate the transition of realized benefits and ongoing measurement to operational management across all programme practices.

narratives.name: Embedding Programme Value into Operational Ownership
narratives.description: Technique for transitioning realized programme benefits into sustained operational management with accountable ownership.

narrativeContexts.context: Benefit transition moves realized benefits from programme management to operational management, ensuring benefits are sustained beyond programme closure through operational embedding rather than merely delivered as project outputs.

Begin transition planning well before programme closure. Assign a named operational owner for each benefit who will be accountable for sustainment after the programme closes. Transfer measurement mechanisms to operational reporting systems. Embed business change activities including training, process changes, organisational adjustments, and cultural shifts rather than merely delivering them. For each benefit, develop sustainment plans specifying how it will be protected from erosion through ongoing measurement, accountable ownership, and integration into business-as-usual operations. Address residual benefits that have not yet materialised at programme closure with specific plans accepted by operational management.

Assuming that delivering capabilities automatically produces benefits without requiring deliberate organisational adoption and change activities. Closing the programme before operational owners have accepted and are resourced for benefit sustainment. Failing to plan for residual benefits that emerge after programme closure, leaving unrealised value without accountability.

patterns.name: Adaptive Programme Lifecycle
patterns.description: Overarching lifecycle orchestrating all 19 alphas across the programme journey.

patternViews.name: Identify and Envision
patternViews.description: Programme opportunity identified and initial vision established.

narrativeContexts.context: A strategic opportunity requiring coordinated multi-project delivery has been identified with an executive sponsor engaged, an initial investment hypothesis articulated, and portfolio governance informed. This prerequisites phase establishes the minimum conditions for programme definition to begin.

patternViews.name: Define and Organize
patternViews.description: Programme formally defined with governance, teams, and roadmap.

narrativeContexts.context: The programme is formally defined with a comprehensive business case, governance structures established, the team-of-teams designed with ART or equivalent structure formed, benefits dependency networks mapped, the roadmap structured into tranches, and cross-project dependencies analyzed. This phase transforms the strategic opportunity into an actionable programme with all four domain practices activated and coordinated.

patternViews.name: Plan and Mobilize
patternViews.description: First tranche mobilized, teams launching, increment planning begins.

narrativeContexts.context: The programme becomes operationally active with the first tranche mobilized, teams beginning coordinated work through the ART or equivalent delivery structure, the first programme increment planned with cross-team objectives and dependencies, and the architectural runway provisioned with initial enablers. Benefits realization planning is complete with baseline measurements established, and governance is functioning at operational cadence.

patternViews.name: Execute and Integrate
patternViews.description: Active delivery through increments with coordination and integration.

narrativeContexts.context: The programme is in full coordinated delivery with programme increments executing on cadence, teams performing with mature coordination mechanisms, dependencies actively managed and resolved, and benefits beginning to emerge as capabilities are delivered and adopted. Cross-practice coordination ensures that strategic value management, capability delivery, team operations, and governance function as an integrated system.

patternViews.name: Realize and Adapt
patternViews.description: Benefits emerging, governance optimizing, roadmap adapting.

narrativeContexts.context: The programme enters the realization phase where the majority of planned benefits are confirmed as achieved, the investment thesis is validated through measurable delivery outcomes, governance mechanisms are optimized through experience, and the roadmap adapts based on delivered results and emerging strategic information. The programme begins its transition with capabilities becoming operational and team structures evolving through continuous inspection and adaptation.

patternViews.name: Transition and Sustain
patternViews.description: Programme transitioning, benefits sustained, teams adjourned.

narrativeContexts.context: The programme formally transitions and closes with realized benefits embedded in operational management through sustainment plans, governance structures dissolved with practices documented as organisational assets, teams adjourned with capabilities and relationships preserved, and the programme's total strategic value contribution confirmed. Organisational learning from the programme lifecycle informs future programme design and the investment thesis is retrospectively validated.
